item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q005_cupredoxin_function_transfer","answer":"SCOPe places all three in the all-beta cupredoxin-like fold (b.6), but not at the same evolutionary level. Plastocyanin/azurin-like proteins are a family within the cupredoxin superfamily (b.6.1); ephrin ectodomains and the PAD4 N-terminal domain are assigned to separate superfamilies in that fold. Thus, the shared classification supports a similar beta-sandwich architecture, not established homology among all three. Copper binding and electron-transfer activity must not be transferred from plastocyanin/azurin templates to ephrins or PAD4: ephrins are extracellular signaling ligands, while PAD4's N-terminal domain is regulatory/noncatalytic rather than a blue-copper electron-transfer domain. Even for another b.6 protein, copper function requires family-level relationship plus conservation of the copper-coordinating site and independent biochemical or spectroscopic evidence. Fold-level representatives may serve as structural templates, but not as functional templates.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
